approach: Add run/ci.rs: the CI branch name, a push and delete (a Git-backed remote behind a small trait), the wait bound and one helper, `with_ci_source`, that returns the source and the wait together. After the candidate is admitted, `check_and_verify` force-pushes it to `athena/ci/<job id>` only for a non-nested run whose origin is an https github.com URL. It calls `resolve` through that helper instead of `NoCi`. With no push the helper gives `NoCi` and a zero-pause single read, so a job with no GitHub remote never waits. `routing::run_routed_recorded` returns the CI record; verification.rs turns it into a `ci-source` entry holding `verify::reuse_statement`. A resumed job rebuilds the record from its resumed CheckRuns whose notes name a CI run. `dispatch` deletes the branch once on every exit after the context exists. `[budget] ci_wait_s` (25 minutes) sets the wait. ci.yml gains the `athena/ci/**` push trigger and a corrected trigger comment. Under cfg(test) the only gh or git push reachable is through the injected seams. With no `ci_seam` installed the CI push is skipped and the source is `NoCi`. Every CI test installs `early_seam` (EarlyFake) and `ci_seam` (recording remote plus a fake `gh::Runner`) and fails on any unexpected gh call.

decisions.choice: Choose the source and the wait together in `with_ci_source(push: Option<&CiPush>, bound_s, f)`. With a push: `GhClient::new(runner, repo).ci_source(&push.branch)` and `ci_wait(bound_s)`. Without: `NoCi` and `Wait { polls: 1, pause: ZERO }`, never reading the bound.
decisions.reason: `read_ci` keeps polling on `Ok(None)` and `NoCi` always returns it, so a 25-minute wait over `NoCi` would sleep in every job with no GitHub remote. One helper makes that pairing impossible.

rejected.why: Every job without a push would sleep 25 minutes before its local checks.

rejected.option: Pick the wait in run/mod.rs beside the call
rejected.why: Leaves two values that a later edit could pair wrongly.

decisions.choice: Tests (critic finding 1): every ci_tests case with a github.com https origin installs both `early_seam` (`test_support::EarlyFake`, as run_pin_tests.rs:424 does) and `ci_seam`. A `ci_run` harness helper installs both and returns guards, so no test can forget one. The EarlyFake log is asserted to hold the early pull request's work-branch push, which shows the two pushes are separate.
decisions.reason: `check_and_verify` calls `early_pr` on every non-nested run, and `early_pr_to` builds the real `GhCli` and `GitRemote` when `early_seam::current()` is empty. The earlier plan installed only `ci_seam`.

rejected.why: The early pull request would make real gh and git push calls.

rejected.option: A global network guard in the test harness
rejected.why: Out of scope; the guard sits in the new code and tests only.

decisions.choice: Fail closed under cfg(test): in ci.rs, when no `ci_seam` is installed, `push_ci_branch` returns None (no push is attempted) and so `with_ci_source` gives `NoCi`. `GitCiRemote` and `GhCli` are built only in non-test builds, except in the one test that drives `GitCiRemote` over a local bare repo (a path, not the network). The fake `gh::Runner` panics on any argument list that is not the runs GET or the jobs GET.
decisions.reason: Existing tests with a github origin (run_pin_tests.rs `early_run`, using GITHUB = https://github.com/owner/repo) now reach `push_ci_branch`. They install no ci_seam, so without this they would run a real `git push` to github.com. The guard test (criterion 3) shows a github origin with early_seam only pushes nothing for CI and falls back locally.

rejected.option: Install ci_seam in every existing test with a github origin
rejected.why: Touches many tests for no behavior gain.

rejected.option: Use the real GitCiRemote when no seam is installed
rejected.why: Real network from the test suite, the failure the critic found.

decisions.choice: A `CiBranchRemote` trait (push, delete) with `GitCiRemote` over `athena_git::Git`; the test-only `ci_seam` carries `Rc<dyn CiBranchRemote>`, `Rc<dyn gh::Runner>` and an optional pause override. `with_ci_source` still builds `GhClient::new(&*runner, repository).ci_source(&ci_branch(id))` under test.
decisions.reason: The branch name, repository and the query (`head_sha`, `event=push`, `branch`) are production code that `Athena::go` runs, so a test can assert the logged query. `gh::Runner` is public (gh/mod.rs re-export).

rejected.why: It replaces the production wiring; a wrong branch would pass.

rejected.option: Add delete to `gh::Remote` and extend early_seam
rejected.why: Needs edits to files that are not deliverables.
Changes gh/client.rs, kept as landed.

decisions.choice: Force-push with the refspec `+<commit>:refs/heads/athena/ci/<id>` through a new `Git::force_push_branch`; delete with `Git::delete_remote_branch`, where an already missing branch is Ok.
decisions.reason: `push_branch` is not forced, so a leftover branch from a killed job at another commit would refuse the push and quietly stop CI reuse. The name belongs to the job alone.

rejected.why: Two network calls and a window with no branch.

decisions.choice: Delete in `dispatch`, around everything built after the `RunContext`, keyed on `ctx.ci_push` being set, on Ok and Err. The reread recursion returns before the context exists, so it never deletes there and the delete happens once.
decisions.reason: One place covers accepted, failed, rejected, early-stop and error exits.

rejected.why: Several callers, and an Err from `produce_and_verify` skips it.

decisions.choice: Hand the verifier the reuse statement as one extra `CheckResultView` named `ci-source`, command 'not a check: where the check results came from', passed true, `detail = verify::reuse_statement(record, sha)`, built in verification.rs like the report-gaps entry.
decisions.reason: `VerifierInputs` and `CheckResultView` live in athena-context (briefs.rs), not a deliverable; changing them touches the brief, budgets and their tests.

rejected.why: Changes athena-context, its budgets and tests.

rejected.option: Name it `ci-result` with command 'not a check'
rejected.why: Reads like a fourth check result.

decisions.choice: Resumed jobs (critic finding 3): when `recorded_checks` is Some, `check_and_verify` calls `ci::record_from_resumed(&runs, &c)`. It returns a `CiRecord { source: Ci }` when at least one resumed CheckRun has a note starting 'result reused from the CI run ' (the text `checks::runs_from_record` writes, checks.rs:125) and names the candidate SHA `c`. The run address is parsed from the note, steps come from the runs' name, passed and duration, and the SHA is `c`. Otherwise it returns None. The result fills `Checked.ci_record`, so the same `ci-source` entry is built. The CHANGELOG says resumed jobs carry the statement.
decisions.reason: The checks come from CI on resume but the record was only filled on a fresh run, so the verifier would see CI-sourced entries with no source statement. The note is the only CI marker stored with the CheckRuns, and rebuilding from it needs no new stored field.

rejected.option: State that a resumed job carries no reuse statement
rejected.why: The verifier would read CI-derived results unlabeled; the brief's criterion 5 requires the statement.

rejected.option: Store the CiRecord on the resume mark
rejected.why: Changes state formats and the record round-trip.

decisions.choice: `routing::run_routed_recorded` returns `(Vec<CheckRun>, Option<CiRecord>)`, the record being Some only when `resolve` returned a record with source Ci. `run_routed` delegates and drops it.
decisions.reason: Existing routing tests keep passing; the caller gets the record for `reuse_statement`.

rejected.why: Breaks callers and tests.

decisions.choice: `[budget] ci_wait_s` is `#[serde(default = ...)] u64` (default 1500) in `Budget`; athena.toml sets 1500. `ci_wait(bound_s)` gives `Wait { pause: 20 s, polls: ceil(bound/20)+1 }`; a bound of 0 gives one poll and a zero pause. Under cfg(test) the pause comes from the seam override when set.
decisions.reason: `Budget` has deny_unknown_fields; the default keeps older configs parsing. `[budget]` already holds `check_timeout_s`.

rejected.why: Breaks configs without the key.
A table for one number.

decisions.choice: Trigger comment (critic finding 2): edit the comment above `on.push` in ci.yml. Branch pushes to `athena/ci/**` run the full checks on Athena's candidate commits in the push cache scope, and Athena's `resolve` reads those runs and reuses a green one. Pushes to pull request branches stay excluded. Only `branches: [main, 'athena/ci/**']` and that comment change.
decisions.reason: The old comment says 'Push runs only for main', which the new trigger contradicts.

rejected.why: Leaves a false comment.

decisions.choice: Aggregate verdict (critic finding 4): the canned jobs reply in both the green and the red test holds a failed `history` job next to the aggregate job ('fmt, clippy, tests' as client.rs names it; the producer copies the exact name from `aggregate_verdict` in gh/client.rs). Green: aggregate job success. Red: aggregate job failed, with the run's own conclusion `failure` and a failed step.
decisions.reason: A real candidate push run has a failing `history` job, so the verdict must come from the aggregate job, not from the run's overall conclusion or from any failed job.

rejected.option: Canned jobs with only successful steps
rejected.why: Would pass even if a failed non-aggregate job wrongly decided the verdict.

decisions.choice: Fallback tests that reach `read_ci` with no usable reply (empty runs, unfinished run, run for another SHA, pull_request-only reply) use `ci_wait_s = 0` or the seam's zero-pause override; one test uses `ci_wait_s = 40` with zero pause and a counting Runner and sees 3 polls.
decisions.reason: `read_ci` keeps polling on `Ok(None)` and on a run for another SHA; only green, red, cancelled, timed_out and a source Err return at once. The default 1500 would sleep.

rejected.option: Leave the default bound in those tests
rejected.why: About 25 minutes each.

decisions.reason: `judge` already reports `check {name} failed` and `reuse_statement` exists (verify.rs:60). The brief keeps client.rs and ci_result.rs as landed.

rejected.why: Not needed.

risks.risk: A job killed before close leaves `athena/ci/<job id>` on the remote.
risks.mitigation: The delete runs on every normal exit, including Err. The push is forced, so a leftover at another commit never blocks a retry (tested). Deleting a missing branch is Ok. No sweeper; the CHANGELOG says so.

risks.risk: Existing tests with a github origin (run_pin_tests.rs) now reach the CI push and could make a real git push.
risks.mitigation: Under cfg(test) `push_ci_branch` returns None when no `ci_seam` is installed, so no GitCiRemote or GhCli is built. A guard test shows it. The new tests always install both seams through `ci_run`.

risks.risk: Adding `ci_wait_s` to athena.toml changes the config hash, so queued readings are read again once.
risks.mitigation: The reread path handles it; the CHANGELOG mentions it.

risks.risk: Tests that reach `read_ci` with no usable reply would sleep for the real 25-minute bound.
risks.mitigation: They use `ci_wait_s = 0` or the zero-pause override; a Wait-values test covers 0 and 1500; one test counts 3 polls at 40 s.

risks.risk: A job with no push inherits the 25-minute wait over `NoCi`.
risks.mitigation: `with_ci_source` returns `NoCi` and the zero-pause single read whenever there is no push and never reads the bound; the criterion 4 test sets 1500 with no override and asserts elapsed under 5 s.

risks.risk: The rebuilt record on resume mislabels a mixed set (some CI, some local) or a note whose wording changes.
risks.mitigation: The rebuild requires the note prefix written by `checks::runs_from_record` and the candidate SHA, and returns None otherwise. A unit test pins the prefix against that function's output, so a wording change fails the test.

risks.risk: A candidate that changes a workflow file pushes a branch the token may refuse, or whose green run `resolve` ignores.
risks.mitigation: `resolve` ignores a green run when a workflow file changed; a refused push is one warning line and the local checks run.

risks.risk: The ci.yml cache is saved only from the default branch, so the first runs on athena/ci/** are cold and may exceed the wait.
risks.mitigation: On timeout `resolve` falls back to the local checks: correct, only slower. The bound is a config value.

risks.risk: The fake Runner's canned JSON could drift from what `pick_ci_run` and `parse_ci_run` expect.
risks.mitigation: The producer builds the JSON in the shape of gh/client.rs and gh/tests.rs; the green test fails if the shape is wrong.

demonstrations.method: Run `Athena::go` on a fake-driver job in a temp repo through the `ci_run` harness helper. Origin is `https://github.com/example/project.git`. Injected: `early_seam::install(EarlyFake, EarlyFake)`, `ci_seam::install(recording remote, fake gh::Runner, zero pause)` and `check_seam` with a counter. The fake Runner answers the runs GET with one finished push run for the pushed commit (success). Its jobs GET returns a failed `history` job plus a successful aggregate job.
demonstrations.observes: The check_seam counter is 0. The logged runs query holds `branch=athena/ci/<job id>`, `event=push` and `head_sha=<the commit the remote was asked to push>`, which is the candidate record's commit. The stored check records have notes naming the CI run address. The committed brief-verifier.md contains the `reuse_statement` text in the `ci-source` entry. The EarlyFake log holds its own work-branch push and no gh call went out other than the two canned GETs.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `NoCi`, or a source for another branch, the counter is 3 or the logged query is wrong. Without the reuse statement the brief assertion fails. If the failed `history` job decided the verdict, the job would not be green.
